claim.qualifier: EPA combined for 2025 Ioniq 5 RWD Long Range (84 kWh battery; 2025 capacity bump from 77.4 kWh)
claim.verbatim_quote: For 2025, this capacity was increased to 84 kWh on long range all-wheel-drive models, which raises the EPA estimate to 290 miles for the SEL AWD trim

reality.qualifier: Consumer Reports 70 mph highway test on AWD Ioniq 5 with prior 77.4 kWh battery measured 267 mi vs 266 EPA at the time. With the 2025 84 kWh upgrade, the gap should be similar in proportion (~8%).
reality.verbatim_quote: We saw 267 miles in our own 70-mph highway range test with our all-wheel drive version equipped with the 77.4 kWh battery.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — 2025 Hyundai Ioniq 5 Road Test Report

narrative_one_liner: Ioniq 5 RWD Long Range 318 mi EPA; CR 70 mph test 267 mi (-16% gap on similar AWD trim).
narrative: Hyundai advertises 318 mi EPA for the 2025 Ioniq 5 RWD Long Range (84 kWh battery, up from 77.4 kWh in prior years). Consumer Reports' 70 mph highway test on the closely-related AWD trim with the older 77.4 kWh battery measured 267 mi against 266 mi EPA at the time — slightly beating EPA in that specific configuration. Recharged synthesis suggests typical 70 mph range for current RWD Long Range is about 250–270 mi (~16% gap from the new 318 figure). The Ioniq 5's boxy crossover shape makes aero drag a notable factor.
methodology_notes: CR's tested unit is the prior-spec AWD with 77.4 kWh; we are inferring the 84 kWh RWD's gap proportionally. Phase 2: re-test with the current 84 kWh trim directly.
caveats: Trim-mismatch: CR tested AWD/77.4 kWh; product record is RWD/84 kWh. Comparing across trim is imprecise.
Recharged synthesis suggests the RWD trim is more efficient than AWD by 5–10%, partially offsetting the boxy-crossover penalty.
Phase 2 should re-test the 2025 84 kWh RWD trim directly for evidence-grade upgrade.
alternative_explanations: Hyundai's 800V architecture optimizes for fast-charging speed at the expense of some efficiency vs. 400V competitors.
Inverter tuning per Out of Spec ('Hyundai did say that... the inverters in this car were tuned more for performance instead of efficiency') may explain the gap.
